title: Affine conormal sections equivalence
statement: Let i : Z → X be a closed immersion of schemes, U an affine open, r : R ≃ Γ(X,U) a ring isomorphism and I = ker(i.app U ∘ r). There exists an r-semilinear equivalence from I/I² to the sections on U of the pushforward of the tensor pullback of i.ker.toModules. It sends the class of every a ∈ I to the adjunction-unit section of the unique ideal-module section whose inclusion equals r(a). The closed immersion, ideal module, module pullback, affine opens and adjunction are those of [def-weil-closed-immersion], [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], [def-pc-module-pullback], [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction].

proof.text: The ideal module i.ker.toModules is the kernel of the structure-module map to the pushforward from its closed subscheme. The structure modules are quasi-coherent; closed-immersion pushforward and quasi-coherent kernels prove quasi-coherence of the ideal module.

*Setting up the affine data.* Write $V=Z\cap U=i^{-1}(U)$ and $\rho:R=\mathcal O_X(U)\to\mathcal O_Z(V)$ for the ring map induced by $i$. The hypothesis $Z\cap U=\operatorname{Spec}(R/I)$ means that $i^{-1}(U)\to U$ is identified over $U$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(R/I)\to\operatorname{Spec}R$; so $V$ is affine, $\mathcal O_Z(V)=R/I$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and $\rho$ is the quotient map $R\to R/I$ (that $V$ is affine with $\rho$ surjective is also [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-affine-cover-criterion] (1), with $I=\ker\rho$). By [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], $\mathcal I(U)=\ker(\mathcal O_X(U)\to\mathcal O_Z(i^{-1}U))=\ker\rho=I$, $\mathcal I|_U=\widetilde I$, and $\mathcal I$ is a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals of $\mathcal O_X$.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 01R3 (lemma-affine-conormal), assertion (2) and its proof ('Mostly clear from the definitions. Note that ... I/I^2 = I \otimes_R R/I. Details omitted.'); Definition 01R2 (definition-conormal-sheaf)

proof.text: *Sections as a tensor product.* Apply [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections] to $f=i:Z\to X$, the quasi-coherent $\mathcal G=\mathcal I$, the affine open $U\subseteq X$ and the affine open $V=i^{-1}(U)\subseteq Z$, with $A=\mathcal O_X(U)=R$, $B=\mathcal O_Z(V)=R/I$ and $\rho$ the quotient map (Step 1): the map $c_{\mathcal I}:\mathcal I(U)\otimes_RB=I\otimes_R(R/I)\to(i^*\mathcal I)(V)=\Gamma(Z\cap U,\mathcal C_{Z/X})$, $a\otimes\bar r\mapsto\bar r\cdot(i^*a)|_V$, is an isomorphism of $R/I$-modules.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 01R3 (lemma-affine-conormal), assertion (2) and its proof ('Mostly clear from the definitions. Note that ... I/I^2 = I \otimes_R R/I. Details omitted.'); Definition 01R2 (definition-conormal-sheaf)

proof.text: *$I\otimes_RR/I=I/I^2$* (the remark in the proof of 01R3). By [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-over-quotient-ring] (1) with $J=I$ and $M=I$, the map $(R/I)\otimes_RI\to I/I\cdot I$, $\bar r\otimes a\mapsto ra\bmod I\cdot I$, is an isomorphism of $R$-modules, where $I\cdot I\subseteq I$ is the submodule generated by the products $ba$ with $b\in I$, $a\in I$; this submodule is exactly the ideal $I^2$, so the target is $I/I^2$. Composing with the swap $I\otimes_R(R/I)\cong(R/I)\otimes_RI$ gives $\tau:I\otimes_R(R/I)\xrightarrow{\sim}I/I^2$, $a\otimes\bar r\mapsto ra\bmod I^2$. Both sides are annihilated by $I$, so the $R$-linear $\tau$ is $R/I$-linear.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 01R3 (lemma-affine-conormal), assertion (2) and its proof ('Mostly clear from the definitions. Note that ... I/I^2 = I \otimes_R R/I. Details omitted.'); Definition 01R2 (definition-conormal-sheaf)

proof.text: *Conclusion.* The composite $c_{\mathcal I}\circ\tau^{-1}:I/I^2\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(Z\cap U,\mathcal C_{Z/X})$ of Steps 3 and 4 sends $a\bmod I^2$ to $(i^*a)|_{Z\cap U}$ for $a\in I=\mathcal I(U)$; it is defined by $i$, $U$ and $\mathcal I$ alone (no choice is made), which is the canonical identification of the statement.

theorem affine_conormal_sections_existence {X Z : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ X)
    [IsClosedImmersion i] :
      ∀ (U : X.affineOpens) (R : Type v) [CommRing R]
        (r : R ≃+* Γ(X, U.1)) (I : Ideal R),
        I = RingHom.ker ((i.app U.1).hom.comp (r : R →+* Γ(X, U.1))) →
        ∃ e : LinearEquiv (r : R →+* Γ(X, U.1))
            (σ' := (r.symm : Γ(X, U.1) →+* R)) I.Cotangent
            Γ((pushforward i).obj ((tensorPullback i).obj i.ker.toModules), U.1),
          ∀ (a : I) (s : Γ(i.ker.toModules, U.1)),
            i.ker.toModulesι.app U.1 s = r (a : R) →
            e (I.toCotangent a) =
              ((Classical.choose (exists_tensorPullbackAdjunction i)).unit.app
                i.ker.toModules).app U.1 s
